title: Cuelight - know the moment your Claude Code agents need you
share: Cuelight is a free Claude Code plugin that tells you the moment an agent is waiting on you, has failed or has gone quiet, and shows the whole multi-agent run behind it: timeline, handoff graph, checks, spend and every prompt. Local, read-only, Python standard library only.
highlights: The problem: multi-agent runs are invisible
Know the moment an agent needs you
Every feature of the dashboard, tab by tab

outro.title: **Cuelight**
outro.sub: Know the moment your agents need you

beats.say: You start five Claude Code agents, switch windows, and ten minutes later find one was waiting on your permission the whole time.
That is the problem with multi-agent work: it is invisible. One scrolling terminal, many agents behind it, and no way to see which one is stuck.
So simple questions go unanswered. Which agent needs me? Did they test their work? What held the run up? And where did the money go?
Cuelight answers them. It reads the transcripts Claude Code already writes and turns them into a live dashboard, on your own machine, read-only.
Here is a live run: thirteen agents shipping a checkout rewrite. The header answers the first question at a glance: running, waiting, failed, and cost against your budget.
Right below it, this bar says Claude is waiting for your permission, so you switch back now, not ten minutes later.
The attention box names every agent that needs a look, and why: unchecked, stalled, retrying, failed, or stuck in a possible loop.

do.label: Who needs a look, and why

beats.say: And when two agents write the same file, Cuelight names both of them, before their edits collide in your merge.
The Pulse strip is a ticker for the run: agents running, tool calls per minute, fresh tokens, and what needs you, each a real series from the transcripts.
Turn on the Pill and a tiny cue light floats over your editor. It sleeps when all is quiet, and hops the moment an agent needs you.
Press Control K and search the whole run. Type unit tests, and the failing test agent and every call it made are right there.
Press Escape, and you are back on the dashboard, with every view one tab away.
The Timeline draws every agent as a bar: when it started, how long it ran, and which wave it belonged to. Outlined bars are the critical path.
The Graph answers who fed whom. Solid edges are exact handoffs, dashed ones are inferred, and every edge opens its evidence.
The Agents tab puts every agent on one row: what it was asked, what its brief said to deliver, and what it actually reported back.
Open any agent for its full story: model, tokens, cost, cache hits, whether it checked its work, and which instruction files it loaded.
Close it, and one click keeps only the agents that need a look, with the reason written on each row.
Insights answers the questions a run raises once it is over. The strip at the top says what each card found, worst first.
The critical path is the chain of agents that set the length of the run. Speeding up any other agent will not finish it sooner.
What the run produced lists the commits, the pull request and every test run, with the cost of each commit.
Did they check their work? For every agent that edited code, Cuelight shows whether it ran a test after its last edit, and whether that passed.
Further down, what went wrong: API stalls, failed calls, retries and timeouts, and the tokens wasted when the prompt cache had to be rebuilt.
Spend shows what the session cost as it ran, the main session and its agents stacked, against your budget line.
Below the chart, the most expensive five minutes and the most expensive agents tell you exactly where the money went.
Prompts ties the cost back to you: each message you sent, how long its work took, and what share of the session it cost.
Activity searches every tool call. Type npm test, and you see which agents ran it, and which runs failed.
The Work Floor shows each agent as a little character, with what it is doing right now, grouped by role or by status.
And Fleet watches all your sessions across projects. The one that needs you sits on top, with Claude Code's own recap of each.

do.label: Every session, the one that needs you first

beats.say: When the run is done, replay it, copy a summary, or export it, and secrets are redacted in everything that leaves.
It even follows your theme, light or dark.
Cuelight is private by design. It listens only on your own machine, needs a token for its data, and makes no network calls at all.
Today it watches Claude Code. Next comes GitHub Copilot CLI, then VS Code and Codex: one control plane for every coding agent you run.
Add it from the plugin marketplace, type slash cuelight open, and know the moment your agents need you.
